document.name: DecisionMirror Project Specification
document.notice: Planning baseline only; does not claim implementation or validation is complete.

project.name: DecisionMirror
project.primary_demo_scenario: Deciding whether to accept an internship opportunity in another city
project.promise: Turn a personal decision into an editable reasoning model, challenge its assumptions, and see how changes affect the reasoning behind it.
project.principle: Help users think better; do not decide for them.

goals: Decompose natural-language decisions into editable reasoning elements.
Expose claims, assumptions, evidence, unknowns, counterarguments, alternatives, and consequences.
Allow users to correct AI-proposed content.
Stress-test assumptions against an immutable baseline.
Trace changes through dependencies and consequences.
Preserve provenance and explain status changes.
non_goals: Choosing a best decision or predicting future outcomes.
Treating system statuses as objective truth.
Replacing professional medical, legal, or financial advice.
Medical diagnosis/treatment, legal strategy, investment/trading, emergencies, or direct physical-safety decisions.
Bayesian probability estimates, unrestricted evidence retrieval, collaboration, or multi-criteria weighting in MVP.

initial_use_cases: Buy an expensive laptop for study or freelance work

workflow.name: Decision Input
workflow.description: User enters decision title, context, and optional alternatives.

workflow.name: Decomposition Review
workflow.description: LLM proposes typed elements; user can accept, edit, reject, add, or delete.

workflow.name: Challenge Center
workflow.description: LLM proposes counterarguments; user reviews each proposal.

workflow.name: Scenario Lab
workflow.description: User changes assumption states to HOLDS or FAILS in a scenario derived from immutable baseline.

workflow.name: Reasoning Map
workflow.description: Displays nodes, relationships, statuses, provenance, and paths.

workflow.name: Decision Report
workflow.description: Traceable summary, supporting arguments, counterarguments, assumptions, evidence gaps, scenario comparison, questions, and next actions.

features.name: Typed Decision Graph
features.note: Soft cap around 40 nodes for MVP.

edge_types.meaning: Evidence or argument supports a claim.
Attack relation evaluated by argumentation engine.
Claim depends on assumption or another claim.
Information gap relevant to target; no status propagation in MVP.
Used for consequence tracing, not direct claim-status assignment.

reasoning_rules.rule: A claim depending on an assumption in FAILS state becomes UNSUPPORTED.
A claim depending on an UNSUPPORTED claim becomes UNSUPPORTED; depending on CHALLENGED or CONDITIONAL makes it at most CONDITIONAL.
Grounded labelling applies to the accepted counterargument graph, not all nodes. An IN counterargument connected by CHALLENGES challenges its claim.
A claim depending on an UNVERIFIED assumption, or lacking at least one supporting evidence item from USER_PROVIDED or EXTERNAL_SOURCE, is at most CONDITIONAL.
Otherwise a claim may be SUPPORTED, subject to higher-priority rules.
SYSTEM_INFERENCE evidence must never independently upgrade a claim to SUPPORTED.
A claim attacked by a PROPOSED counterargument gets challenged_by_unverified_counterargument flag; proposal does not change status.

argumentation.IN: All attackers are OUT, or there are no attackers.
argumentation.OUT: At least one attacker is IN.
argumentation.UNDECIDED: Neither IN nor OUT condition holds.
argumentation.notes: Only USER_ACCEPTED counterarguments are eligible. Review state is distinct from grounded label.

evaluation_semantics.dependency_direction: Store dependent claim -> prerequisite; use reverse dependency index to find dependents.

propagation.SUPPORTS: Changes to supporting evidence/argument trigger target claim reevaluation.
propagation.DEPENDS_ON: Propagate through reverse dependencies in deterministic topological order.
propagation.ATTACKS: Triggers argumentation reevaluation, not ordinary dependency propagation.
propagation.CHALLENGES: Review/label changes trigger target claim reevaluation.
propagation.LEADS_TO: Trace consequences; do not directly set claim status.
propagation.ADDRESSES: No claim-status propagation semantics in MVP.

scenario_pipeline: Evaluate affected claims in deterministic topological order with stable ID tie-break
Produce status/impact diff and causal paths
evaluation_semantics.baseline: Every scenario references one immutable baseline version. Editing baseline creates a new version and marks scenarios on old version stale.

cycles.LEADS_TO: Reject in MVP unless explicit semantics are designed
cycles.ATTACKS: Allowed and handled by grounded labelling

consequence_mapping.note: For multiple upstream claims, derive impact from all relevant sources. Never say SAFE.

may: Generate concise explanations and report wording
llm_contract.evidence_policy: URL existence, source trustworthiness, and support for a claim are separate properties. MVP has no unrestricted LLM web search.

architecture.llm: External provider adapter selected based on current cost, latency, structured-output reliability, and retention policy.
architecture.repository_compliance: Public GitHub repo, open-source license, .kiro at repository root and not ignored. Folder names beyond explicit organizer requirements are engineering recommendations.

constraints: Validate endpoint membership in same version
unresolved: Copy nodes/edges per version or immutable snapshots with membership
Persist evaluation runs or recompute on read

security_privacy: Anonymous/private sessions with strict resource isolation
HttpOnly and Secure production cookies; appropriate SameSite
CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints
Rate-limit LLM endpoints and enforce input size limits
Do not log decision text, prompts, or sensitive reports
Keep API keys server-side; do not expose PostgreSQL publicly
Support and test user data deletion
Review provider retention/training policies before sending user content

deployment.profile_note: Starting point for measurement, not a capacity guarantee.
reliability: No false success when database writes fail
deployment.performance_note: Targets are proposed budgets, not measured results.

test_suites: LLM reliability and prompt injection SEC01-SEC15

submission_checks: Recheck deadline, timezone, judging period, prizes, and eligibility on live organizer rules
open_decisions: Choose LLM provider based on current price, latency, structured output, and retention terms
Define session expiry and backup retention
Confirm installed Kiro version's exact spec/steering/hook/agent formats
